Mechatronik's New M SEC 630 Reimagines the C126 With 6.2-liter AMG Naturally Aspirated V8 Muscle
14 photos
Photo: Mechatronik
Mercedes specialist Mechatronik is building 30 examples of the M SEC 630, and the process obviously starts by stripping 30 existing SECs down to bare metal. Rebuilt around the AMG division's naturally aspirated M156 engine, the ultra-limited model remains a C126 where it actually matters, VIN included.
The project marks the German company's 30th anniversary in 2027, and it further serves as the third entry in the New Tech Series. Following the modernized SL and M twins, the C126-based model spent more than four years in development. In essence, Mechatronik remained faithful to the Bruno Sacco design while giving the rear-biased thriller considerably more contemporary running gear.
Under the hood, the M156 is the perfect choice for this vehicle. AMG 's final production naturally aspirated V8 sounds a lot better than current bi-turbo mills, and 500 ps (493 hp) is plenty enough for this application. Delivered at 5,200 revolutions per minute, peak torque is estimated at 630 Nm (465 lb-ft) by the Pleidelsheim-based outfit.
By comparison, the C 63 AMG Black Series from the 204 series made 517 ps (510 hp) and 620 Nm (457 lb-ft) with the right kind of dinosaur juice in the fuel tank. The M SEC 630 delivers the goodies to its rear axle by means of a limited-slip differential and the AMG SPEEDSHIFT version of the 7G-TRONIC box.
Prospective customers are presented with a custom-designed stainless exhaust with sport cats, an optional performance exhaust, or a race option. Unfortunately, the loudest one is available only for certain export markets. The M156 chosen by Mechatronik gives the M SEC 630 a more traditional relationship between the driver's throttle input and how the engine responds, whereas the 7G transmission keeps the car usable for long-distance grand touring.
Photo: Mechatronik As far as the body shell is concerned, the restomod comes with new bumpers, fenders, skirts, cladding, and a rear spoiler, all of them crafted from carbon fiber. The rear wheel arch extensions use steel construction. At both ends, LED modules do the talking. Mechatronik quotes illumination distances of 180 meters (591 feet) for the dipped beams and 380 meters (1,247 feet) for the highs.
Customers may also retain the original front and rear lights. Coilover suspension with Dual Flow Valve technology from Ohlins also needs mentioning, whereas the stopping power comes from Brembo. The standard brakes use two-piece discs, while cars equipped with the GT package upgrade to larger front discs, braided steel brake lines, and performance-oriented brake pads.
Speaking of said package, going for the GT also means a dry weight reduction of 88 kilos, from the standard 1,712 kilograms (3,774 pounds) to 1,624 kilograms (3,589 pounds). Mechatronik further highlights that GT-equipped models are faster in a straight line, raising the electronic limiter from 250 kilometers per hour (155 miles per hour) to 280 kilometers per hour (174 miles per hour).
That's not all, though. Acceleration figures also differ, with Mechatronik claiming 4.2 and 4.0 seconds flat, respectively, from naught to 100 kilometers per hour (62 miles per hour). To achieve its weight reduction, the GT specification drops the rear seats. 19-inch wheels in two designs are on the menu, whereas tire choices include Michelin's Pilot Sport 4 S and the stickier Pilot Sport Cup 2.
Retaining the original dash architecture of the C126 , the M SEC 630 sweetens the deal with different leather finishes, carpeting, stitching, headliners, veneers, and everything in between, including carbon-fiber buckets from Recaro.
The infotainment system avoids forcing a tablet into the middle of the dash, with customers offered a 1-DIN unit called Radio Classic. And finally, the most serious audio system available offers 10 speakers, 3 subs, and 1,560 watts. View this post on Instagram A post shared by MECHATRONIK (@mechatronik)
